concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Earth's rotation about its axis through the North and South Poles, from West to East, in about 24 hours.
Explain that the Sun appears to move from East to West across the sky because the Earth rotates from West to East.
Explain how the Earth's rotation causes the cycle of day and night, with half the Earth lit at any time.
Use the West-to-East rotation to explain why sunrise occurs earlier in eastern places than in western ones.

topics.title: Apparent motion of the stars and the Moon

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Pole Star appears nearly stationary while other stars appear to move around it.
Recognise the Foucault pendulum and Aryabhata's boat analogy as ways of understanding the Earth's rotation.

topics.title: Revolution of the Earth and the changing night sky

concepts.learning_objective: Define revolution and orbit and state that the Earth revolves around the Sun in about 365 days and 6 hours.
Explain why the stars seen after sunset change gradually over a year as the Earth revolves.
Explain how the tilt of the Earth's axis and its spherical shape cause seasons, reversed in the two hemispheres.
Identify the solstices and equinoxes and the length of daytime on them in the Northern Hemisphere.
Explain how apparent size depends on actual size and distance, so the Moon can cover the Sun.
Describe the arrangement of the Sun, Moon and Earth in total and partial solar eclipses.
State safe and unsafe ways of viewing a solar eclipse.
Describe the arrangement of the Sun, Earth and Moon during a lunar eclipse.
Describe how total and partial lunar eclipses appear and that they are safe to watch.
